Fireflies use bioluminescence to communicate and attract mates: flash patterns are species-specific, males fly and flash in a pattern, receptive females flash back, and the back-and-forth continues until they meet and mate. Fireflies also flash brightly to startle predators and make them drop prey. #bioluminescence #fireflies
Firefly flashing is innate and energy-efficient; it is unlikely fireflies experience mental fatigue or frustration from flashing to attract mates. #bioluminescence #fireflies

Animals other than fireflies that use bioluminescence for communication/attraction: deep-sea fish (communicate, attract prey or mates, avoid predators), some jellyfish, squids and octopuses, glowworms (attract mates, lure prey), and some fungi (attract spore-dispersing insects). #bioluminescence

Practical human applications of bioluminescence: biomarker/biosensor detection (proteins, DNA, disease and pollution diagnosis), bioluminescent imaging using luciferase to study living cells and gene expression, energy-efficient lighting, and glow-in-the-dark paints/materials. #bioluminescence #technology
